candidates.name: AiguaDeBarcelona_DataChallenge
candidates.what_it_holds: Barcelona water utility (Aigües de Barcelona) data-challenge repo: water consumption measured by meter, broken out by industrial / domestic / tourism-sector use, by geographical region within Barcelona, for 2019-2021 (pre/post-COVID span). Repo structure has db/, model/, src/, app.py (Flask), requirements.txt; described as analysing consumption 'by industrial, domestic and tourism factors using AI'. Apache-2.0 licensed. Exact row/column counts and CSV filenames not confirmed by the fetch (would need a clone to see db/ contents).
candidates.why_useful: Barcelona is one of our 13 held Inside Airbnb panel cities. A tourism-sector water-consumption series by district, spanning a COVID collapse and recovery, is a genuine independent occupancy proxy for a market we already track — directly on-theme for 'utility consumption as occupancy proxy' and could cross-check the Barcelona Inside Airbnb reviews-based stays index.
candidates.size_hint: unknown row count; multi-year meter-level utility data by sector/region

candidates.name: TOTA-Water-Consumption-PowerBI-Dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed water_data.csv plus a tota_water_consumption_dashboard.pbix (Power BI) for the Okanagan watershed pilot region (Thompson Okanagan Tourism Association, British Columbia, Canada), built for that region's annual UN Tourism INSTO (International Network of Sustainable Tourism Observatories) reporting. Multi-municipality, multi-year municipal water consumption data collected from public sources; supports year-over-year comparison. No license file found.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, tourism-board-curated municipal water-consumption CSV explicitly built for a UN Tourism sustainable-tourism observatory report is a rare direct water-as-tourism-activity proxy, and demonstrates the INSTO reporting format that other tourism regions may also publish on GitHub.
candidates.time_coverage: multi-year, exact range not stated in README excerpt

candidates.name: popFlowEstonia
candidates.what_it_holds: Population flowmap built from mobile-positioning-data OD (origin-destination) matrices sourced from the University of Tartu Mobility Lab — the same academic group behind Positium and much of the Eurostat 'mobile positioning data for tourism statistics' (MNO) pilot work. Repo has a data/ folder plus a leaflet-based web map (index.html, js/, leaflet/). Exact file contents/format not confirmed (fetch could not enumerate data/ folder contents or confirm real vs. demo data).
candidates.why_useful: Directly downstream of the Estonian mobile-positioning/MNO tourism-statistics ecosystem the Eurostat experimental series is built on; if the OD matrices in data/ are real (not synthetic demo), this is a rare committed MNO-derived mobility dataset rather than just a paper describing the method.
candidates.size_hint: unknown; small repo (README + data folder + web map)

candidates.name: FlowKit
candidates.what_it_holds: Flowminder's open-source CDR (call detail record) analytics toolkit: a full pipeline (Spark backend, FlowAPI, FlowClient Python/R clients, FlowAuth) for turning raw mobile operator CDRs into mobility indicators (flows, residential/relocation, subscriber density, event counts) at scale. No data committed (operates on an operator's own CDR store) but a mature, actively maintained (98 stars, updated Aug 2026), MPL-2.0-licensed method for exactly the kind of MNO-derived mobility indicator Eurostat's experimental tourism statistics use.
candidates.why_useful: This is the reference open-source implementation of the MNO-mobility-indicator pipeline (used in real national statistics offices for humanitarian/mobility work); documents the exact indicator definitions (home location, trips, subscriber density) that a from-scratch MNO tourism proxy would need, even though we would still need our own CDR/roaming source to run it.
candidates.geography: global (framework, not tied to one country)

candidates.name: Positium-Data-Platform
candidates.what_it_holds: A modular, Dockerized pipeline (Spark for compression, PostGIS for spatial joins, Flask REST API) for processing 'mobile event data' into hourly-event counts, user-movement, and population-distribution outputs — an independent reimplementation of the Positium-style MNO data pipeline (Positium is Eurostat's MNO tourism-statistics pilot contractor). No data committed; needs a raw mobile-event feed to run.
candidates.why_useful: Gives working, inspectable code for exactly the kind of MNO event-to-population-distribution pipeline Eurostat's experimental tourism series is built on, useful if the team ever gets access to any roaming/CDR feed (even a small national one) to nowcast visitor presence.

candidates.name: mobilib
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library for processing and modelling mobile positioning data (OD matrix construction, spatial interaction / gravity models, delineation of functional regions from mobility data). MIT licensed, no committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose method library for turning raw mobile-positioning feeds into interpretable mobility/OD statistics; relevant if the team obtains any MNO-derived feed for a tourism market.

candidates.name: SynthMPDGenerator
candidates.what_it_holds: A program for generating synthetic mobile positioning data (MPD), from the same Estonian/Tartu mobile-positioning research cluster as popFlowEstonia and MPDSamplingStatistics. No real data; generates synthetic test data for MPD-based methods.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only for testing an MNO-tourism-proxy pipeline before real data is available; not itself a data source.

candidates.name: MPDSamplingStatistics
candidates.what_it_holds: A program for comparing different Mobile Positioning Data (MPD)-based results against each other with statistical tests — companion tool to SynthMPDGenerator from the same Estonian mobility-lab ecosystem underlying Eurostat's MNO tourism-statistics pilot.
candidates.why_useful: Methodological reference for validating any MNO-derived tourism/mobility proxy the team might build; no data itself.

candidates.name: Mobile_data_analysis (CDR-Based Tourism Analytics in Rwanda)
candidates.what_it_holds: A single script (CDR_analysis.py) plus LICENSE — no data committed. Described as leveraging Call Detail Records (CDR) and ML to analyze tourist mobility patterns, visitor flows, and economic impact in Rwanda; almost certainly built against the well-known 'Data for Development' (D4D) Rwanda mobile-operator CDR dataset (MTN Rwanda / NISR), which is not itself in this repo and requires a separate data-use application to the original challenge organizers.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms a working CDR-to-tourism-mobility methodology exists for at least one country's real operator CDR release (Rwanda D4D), which is the closest real-world analogue to an MNO tourism-statistics pipeline; the underlying D4D Rwanda dataset itself (external, application-gated) would be the actual find if pursued.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified (D4D Rwanda challenge data, ~2013-2016 vintage typically)
candidates.size_hint: code only; underlying CDR dataset external and access-gated

candidates.name: Sustainable-Tourism-Impact-in-Decision-Support-System
candidates.what_it_holds: Small student project analysing tourism sustainability metrics (Total Revenue from Tourism, Tourism Employment Rate, Carbon Footprint Per Tourist, Waste Generated Per Tourist, Resident Satisfaction Index, Water Consumption per Tourist, GDP Contribution from Tourism, Sustainability Policy Compliance) via Excel then Power BI. Geography/time period not confirmed; appears to be a coursework-style dataset, possibly synthetic or a compiled multi-country panel.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying panel is real (not illustrative), 'Waste Generated Per Tourist' and 'Water Consumption per Tourist' are exactly the utility/waste occupancy-proxy metrics this theme targets, across what may be a cross-country panel — worth a closer look to confirm data provenance.

candidates.name: MyEuroStatApp
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source Kotlin Multiplatform mobile/desktop client for the public Eurostat API, with a dedicated tourism module alongside economy, population, environment, trade, social, and science modules. AGPL-3.0 licensed, updated 4 Sep 2026 (actively maintained). No data committed; it is a generic Eurostat-API pull client.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, general-purpose Eurostat API client that already has a tourism module could be adapted to pull MNO-derived experimental tourism tables (or the tour_ce_omr series we already hold) programmatically, though it duplicates a pull mechanism rather than adding new data.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Eurostat tour_ce_omr platform nights pull (we already have this series; this is just another API client)

candidates.name: reverse-engineering-YJMob100K-grid
candidates.what_it_holds: Code 'revealing urban area from mobile positioning data' by reverse-engineering the spatial grid underlying YJMob100K, a large (100,000-user, ~90-day) human mobility dataset released by Yahoo Japan / LY Corporation for a 2024 mobility-prediction challenge (data itself hosted externally, not in this repo). BSD-3-Clause.
candidates.why_useful: Points to YJMob100K as an external, sizeable Japan urban-mobility dataset derived from mobile positioning; not tourism-labeled but could proxy visitor movement in a market (Japan/APAC) that is one of our numbered regional gaps if cross-referenced with known tourist areas.
candidates.time_coverage: ~90-day panel, dataset released for a 2024 challenge
candidates.size_hint: external dataset: 100,000 users x ~90 days of location records (YJMob100K, hosted by the challenge organizers, not in this repo)
candidates.license: BSD-3-Clause (for this repo's code; YJMob100K itself has its own terms)

notes: Modality was badly constrained: WebSearch reported the session-wide 200-query budget was already exhausted before I ran a single query (shared across all scouts in this sweep), and every fallback search-engine scrape via WebFetch (html.duckduckgo.com, lite.duckduckgo.com, ecosia.org) returned HTTP 403. Bing (bing.com/search) did load via WebFetch but its results were poor for multi-term/site: queries -- WebFetch's summarizer consistently reported only generic github.com navigation pages or unrelated literal-keyword matches (e.g. 'D4D' matched a shopping app, 'mobile network operator' matched carrier homepages), suggesting Bing's SERP either wasn't rendering fully for the fetcher or genuinely has thin GitHub coverage for these niche phrases. Google search likewise returned only the JS-shell page, no results. The productive channel ended up being `gh search repos` (keyword, not site:), which is not the primary channel this modality specifies but was explicitly permitted as a fallback -- however it hit the shared GitHub API rate limit (403) repeatedly, cutting short planned searches on electricity+occupancy, waste+tourism, and smart-meter+London/housing before they returned results. Given more budget I would: (1) clone/inspect AiguaDeBarcelona_DataChallenge's db/ and popFlowEstonia's data/ folders directly to confirm real vs. demo data and exact row counts; (2) search specifically for 'REFIT', 'Pecan Street Dataport', 'Low Carbon London' smart-meter repos cross-referenced against known short-term-rental-heavy postcodes; (3) search for Balearic Islands / Mallorca and Lisbon municipal water/waste open-data portals with GitHub mirrors, since both are major tourist markets; (4) retry the MNO/roaming-data and waste-generation gh queries once the rate limit resets. No repo found here mentions Airbnb by name in a utility-data context -- the two solid utility hits (Barcelona water, Okanagan water) are general tourism-sector consumption, and the MNO/CDR hits are mostly Estonia-ecosystem tooling with no committed large real-world dataset confirmed.
